chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Muhraz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I do not pray over the one drowned in wine.'

key_terms.غَرِيقِ خَمْرٍ: One drowned in wine (died from excessive consumption)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing funeral prayer for a wine drinker who dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the specific juristic ruling that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) would withhold funeral prayer (*Salat al-Janazah*) from a *Gharig al-Khamr*—one who dies while intoxicated or due to wine consumption. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted not as a denial of their faith, but as a distinct sign of divine displeasure and a deterrent, emphasizing the severity of the sin of intoxication compared to other major sins.
